Why This Matters

The CDC says kids ages 6 to 17 need at least 60 minutes of active time each day. That time should range from brisk to hard effort. CDC

The CDC also calls for muscle and bone work. Kids ages 6 to 17 should do this at least 3 days a week. CDC

NCES lists 333 students in the local district for 2024 to 2025. The district spans pre-K through grade 12. A coached class can be one part of a child's active week. NCES

This Week's Curriculum

  • The Guard Matrix
  • Defending the Back Ride
  • Attacking from Closed Guard
  • Standing Up from Closed Guard

Links Learn the class words.

The Vale-Tudo / closed-guard theme: "Whoever manages the distance manages the damage." Gracie Academy

Defending the Back Ride: The 2024 IBJJF rules give 4 points for back control. You must hold it for 3 seconds and meet the grip and leg rules. IBJJF Rules (UFAF mirror)

Attacking from Closed Guard: A sweep from guard or half guard can earn 2 points. You must hold top control for 3 seconds under the rules. IBJJF Rules (UFAF mirror)

Standing Up from Closed Guard: The sweep rule can include a move from guard to your feet. You must meet the rule's control terms. Ask your coach to check the full rule. IBJJF Rules (UFAF mirror)

senseisandy.com | (917) 736-8649 | Studio location

What EBI-Style Overtime Means

The event plan used EBI-style rules. A hold or escape can decide the result. If the main round ends level, students start extra time from set positions.

FloGrappling describes a 10-minute main round. A tap can end the round. Extra time starts from back control or an armbar position called spiderweb. Each athlete takes a turn to attack and escape. If both escape, the time can decide the winner. FloGrappling

Submission Challenge lists one extra round for bracket matches. Finals may use up to 3 extra rounds. Each event sets its own rules. Submission Challenge See 12-week program pricing.
